title: Twist Germany Readiness
subtitle: Grades 1 and 2 are written for German children; grades 3 and 4 are mostly English copies or empty stubs, and the English and Math tracks are not yet shaped for German schools.

verdict.label: Not ready
verdict.basis: Mean of the ten area scores (26 of 50, so 52 out of 100) minus 12 because the weakest findings hit two of the four grades and the English track.
verdict.headline: Twist can launch grades 1 and 2 in German after a few fixes, but the full G1 to G4 range is not ready for Germany.
summary: In the German-instruction folder (de/), all 93 German and about 83 of 86 Math lesson parts in grade 1, and the same share in grade 2, are written in natural German with teaching before practice, three-tier hints and per-answer feedback.

Grade 3 is mostly placeholders (192 of its 316 lesson files have a placeholder opener and a narration of just a full stop), and grade 4 Math and English read as English with US number formats, dollars and inches.

Content gaps that German teachers check first are missing: spelling strategies, syllable reading, timed reading, joined handwriting, and any link to the KMK standards or VERA-3. English is built as first-language literacy, not as the foreign language German schools teach.
A launch of grades 1 and 2 (German and Math) is realistic once US money is replaced with euro and the standards mapping exists; grades 3 and 4 need real authoring first.
conditions: Replace the 192 placeholder lesson parts and the English text in G3 and G4 Math and English with authored German, or hide those grades at launch.
Localise Math to Germany: euro and cent instead of Pennys, Nickel and dollars; metric only; German number formats (3.847, not 3,847).
Decide the English offer: a foreign-language English track (vocabulary, listening, speaking) for G3 and G4, or remove English from the German launch.
Add a German spelling-strategy and syllable-reading strand, plus a mapping of every lesson to a KMK area and a state curriculum, so schools can see the fit.
Offer a Schreibschrift option (or state clearly that only Druckschrift is taught) and decide which state scripts to support.

Fix the placeholder hints (1,160 of 1,832 G3 and 876 of 1,723 G4 guided-practice questions) and complete the German audio (the repo notes say German audio upload waits on a storage-key fix) before any paid release.

reviewed: Six benchmark crosswalks were opened; the three for the German instruction language (German, Math, English) were read in full for their summaries and key tables.
Research notes: german-insight, type-gaps, mechanics-benchmark, calibration, media-benchmark, anatomy, FINDINGS (all in /Users/diemu/ist/b2c/rnd).
Twist docs: docs/CLAUDE.md, docs/specs/assessment.md (key sections), docs/authoring/german-en-loi-standard.md, docs/authoring/item-quality-rules.md, docs/notes/ship-decisions.md.
All 12 de/ module catalogs (grades 1 to 4, three subjects); structure and lesson titles.

Whole de/ tree scanned by script: 1,216 lesson parts, 397 assessments, 3,151 skill-practice banks, 372 practice sets (language, hint and placeholder counts are my own word-list checks, not a human read).
About 12 lesson-part files read by hand across G1 German, G1 Math, G1 English, G3 German, G3 Math, G4 German, G4 Math.
not_reviewed: No audio or images were listened to or viewed; audio and picture quality are not judged.
No learner or teacher testing; no live app run.
The three crosswalks for the English instruction language were not read beyond the summary in german-insight.
State curricula (Lehrplan documents) were not read; only the standards list supplied with the brief was used.
Language shares come from a word-list heuristic; short numeric items can be misread, so counts are approximate.
Whether the app renders all 19 question types seen in the content is unverified.

standards.name: KMK Bildungsstandards Deutsch, Primarbereich (revised 23.06.2022)
standards.requires: Four areas by end of Klasse 4: Sprechen und Zuhören; Schreiben; Lesen; Sprachgebrauch und Sprachwissen untersuchen. Binding in all 16 states.

standards.name: KMK Bildungsstandards Mathematik, Primarbereich
standards.requires: Five Leitideen (Zahlen und Operationen; Raum und Form; Muster und Strukturen; Größen und Messen; Daten, Häufigkeit und Wahrscheinlichkeit) plus process competences (Problemlösen, Kommunizieren, Argumentieren, Modellieren, Darstellen).

standards.name: VERA-3 comparison tests
standards.requires: National tests in Klasse 3 built on the KMK standards; schools and parents read results against them.

standards.name: State Lehrpläne (for example LehrplanPLUS Bavaria, NRW Lehrpläne)
standards.requires: Each state has its own curriculum; the KMK standards are the common floor, so content must be mappable per state.

standards.name: Primary English as a foreign language
standards.requires: Starts in Klasse 3 in most states (Klasse 1 in Brandenburg, Hamburg, Rheinland-Pfalz; Baden-Württemberg and NRW moved back to Klasse 3) and is taught as a foreign language.

standards.name: Handwriting scripts
standards.requires: All states start with unjoined print script; the joined script (Lateinische Ausgangsschrift, Schulausgangsschrift, Vereinfachte Ausgangsschrift, Grundschrift) varies by state.

standards.name: German as a second language (DaZ)
standards.requires: A separate track from native-speaker Deutsch, levelled by CEFR (A1, A2). Verified 2026-10-09 per the review brief; no URL was supplied.

areas.name: Lesen lernen (decoding)
areas.subject: German
areas.standard: Lesen area of kmk-de: secure letter-sound links, syllable reading, fluent word and sentence reading in Klasse 1 and 2.
areas.twist_today: G1 has authored letter, letter-sound, short-vowel, umlaut and consonant lessons (A to Z with the German sounds), then one-sentence reading with Wer, Was, Wo, Wann. G2 adds vowels, clusters, word families. Reading comprehension continues to G4.
areas.finding: The letter-sound work is well made and German-native. Syllable reading, syllable marking and timed word reading, which German teachers use to build fluency, are not in Twist.

areas.fix: Add a syllable strand (Silben klatschen, mark, read) and a timed word-reading mode on the existing choose-one type; reuse the G1 letter-sound lessons as the base.

areas.name: Rechtschreibung (spelling strategies)
areas.subject: German
areas.standard: Schreiben area of kmk-de: pupils spell with strategies (Silbenschwingen, Verlängern, Ableiten, Merkwörter) and use a dictionary.
areas.twist_today: Spelling shows up as phonics, word families, compounds, affixes, punctuation and capitalization. No lesson named for a spelling strategy exists in the catalogs.
areas.finding: Strategy-based spelling is the backbone of Klasse 2 and 3 in the benchmark and is the most visible hole for teachers and parents.

areas.fix: Author a Rechtschreibstrategien unit for G2 to G4 (swing syllables, lengthen, derive, Merkwörter, dictionary) with new skill banks and finals.

areas.name: Schreiben und Sprachgebrauch (writing and grammar)
areas.subject: German
areas.standard: Schreiben and Sprachgebrauch areas of kmk-de: plan, write and revise texts; name word classes and sentence parts.
areas.twist_today: G3 and G4 catalogs list noun gender, Nominativ and Akkusativ, Perfekt, plurals, Dativ, Präteritum, adjective endings, essay, letter and opinion writing. G4 files are written in German; G3 files are mostly placeholders.
areas.finding: Breadth is good and in places earlier than the benchmark, but word classes, sentence types, adjective comparison and Satzglieder drills are absent, and the G3 files are empty shells.

areas.name: Handwriting (Druckschrift and Schreibschrift)
areas.subject: German
areas.standard: handwriting: unjoined print script everywhere; a joined script that differs by state.
areas.twist_today: One G1 lesson on Druckschrift letter shapes and spacing, with 22 tracing items across all de/ lessons. No joined script lesson anywhere.
areas.finding: Print script is covered; the joined script is absent, and which script is taught is a state decision Twist does not yet expose.

areas.name: Math coverage and progression
areas.subject: Math
areas.standard: kmk-math: all five Leitideen by end of Klasse 4, with number ranges 20, 100, 1,000 and 1,000,000 over the four years.
areas.twist_today: 137 lessons across G1 to G4: counting and operations to 1,000,000, multiplication tables, written methods, fractions, decimals, geometry, measurement, data and probability, in the same order as the German years.
areas.finding: Content coverage is close to the German sequence (135 of 137 lessons match). It runs a year later on multiplication tables, and Zahlenmauern, Rechentabellen and Nachbaraufgaben are absent.

areas.name: Math in a German context
areas.subject: Math
areas.standard: kmk-math (Größen und Messen): euro and cent, metric units, local number formats.
areas.twist_today: G1 money lessons teach Penny, Nickel, Dime and Quarter in German sentences; G2 to G4 use dollars; G4 teaches inches and miles; G3 and G4 numbers are written with US commas.
areas.finding: US currency and imperial units in a German-language product is the kind of error teachers and parents notice in the first lesson.

areas.name: English as a foreign language
areas.subject: English
areas.standard: english-fl: foreign-language English from Klasse 3 (Klasse 1 in three states): listening, speaking, themed vocabulary, simple sentences.
areas.twist_today: de/ English is first-language literacy with German instructions: letter recognition, short-vowel phonics, word families, sight words, paragraph and essay writing, grammar, research and media skills.
areas.finding: A German parent expects hello, colours, family, school and speaking practice. Twist teaches how an English native speaker learns to read, which does not match the school curriculum.

areas.name: Lesson design and exercise variety
areas.subject: All
areas.standard: Common practice in German learning apps and schools: teach, then practise, with varied tasks and feedback.
areas.twist_today: Every part runs opener, warmup, teach, guided practice, applied practice, challenge, assessment. 19 question types are in use, including tracing, matching, sorting, ordering, audio choice and clock hands.
areas.finding: The design is stronger than the benchmark on teaching first and scaffolded hints. Gaps are read-a-passage-then-answer, tap-on-picture, column-arithmetic grids and speaking that is switched on.

areas.name: Assessment and standards alignment
areas.subject: All
areas.standard: vera3 and kmk-de/kmk-math: results are read against KMK competence areas; schools use VERA-3 as the Klasse 3 yardstick.
areas.twist_today: Each grade has 3 baseline and 3 final grade assessments per subject, plus slot-based lesson finals (8 to 15 slots, no hints, retake variety). No lesson or slot is tagged with a KMK area or state curriculum.
areas.finding: The design is solid and can carry a mapping; the mapping itself does not exist, so a teacher cannot see which Kompetenzbereich a result belongs to.

strengths.title: Teaching comes before practice, every time
strengths.detail: Every part has a teach step with worked examples, while the benchmark teaches only where an author added a screen.

strengths.title: Three-tier hints on every guided question
strengths.detail: All 7,460 guided-practice questions in de/ carry three hints; G1 and G2 hints read as real scaffolds.

strengths.title: Natural German in G1 and G2
strengths.detail: Items read as written for German children (sounds, umlauts, ß, Wer/Was/Wo/Wann) with feedback on each wrong option.

strengths.title: Assessment design
strengths.detail: Grade baseline and final, slot-based lesson finals, no hints, retake variety; the benchmark has only a lesson test.

strengths.title: Speaking interaction exists in the model
strengths.detail: The benchmark has no speaking item at all; Twist has one, though it is switched off in all 35 current instances.

priorities.action: Decide the launch scope: ship G1 and G2 German and Math first, and hide G3 and G4 until authored.
priorities.why: Two of four grades are placeholders or English; this removes the largest launch risk quickly.

priorities.action: Localise Math money, units and number formats for Germany in G1 to G4.
priorities.why: US coins and dollars in German text are visible in the first lesson.

priorities.action: Author G3 German (64 placeholder parts) and G3 and G4 Math to the G1 and G3 diphthong standard, then their practice banks.
priorities.why: This is the content that fills the missing grades.

priorities.action: Decide the English offer for Germany and build a foreign-language track for G3 and G4.
priorities.why: The current literacy lessons do not match what German schools teach.

priorities.action: Tag every skill and slot with KMK areas and a state curriculum, and publish a coverage page.
priorities.why: Teachers and schools ask for the link to the standards and to VERA-3.

priorities.action: Build a spelling-strategy and syllable-reading strand for G1 to G4.
priorities.why: The most visible curriculum hole for German teachers and parents.

priorities.action: Add a Schreibschrift option and tracing lessons for the main state scripts.
priorities.why: Joined handwriting is part of Klasse 2 in most states.

priorities.action: Add read-a-passage and tap-on-picture item types and switch speaking on.
priorities.why: Closes the main exercise-type gaps found in the benchmark.

method: Read the research crosswalks and notes in /Users/diemu/ist/b2c/rnd, then the Twist docs, catalogs and a scripted scan of every de/ JSON file.
Opened about 12 lesson-part files by hand across G1, G3 and G4 to confirm the language, the item quality and what the scan counts mean.
Market comparisons come from a lesson-by-lesson study of a leading German learning app's full curriculum, used for inspiration only.
German standards come from the brief (verified 2026-10-09); no standards were re-fetched. Counts marked as my scan are keyword and word-list checks, not human reads.

glossary.meaning: Deutsch als Zweitsprache: German as a second language for children who do not speak it at home, levelled A1 and A2.
Spelling strategies such as Silbenschwingen (swing the syllables), Verlängern (lengthen the word), Ableiten (derive) and Merkwörter (words to memorise).
Unjoined print script and the joined handwriting taught from Klasse 2; the joined version differs by state.
National goals for the end of Klasse 4 agreed by all 16 states; each state then writes its own Lehrplan.
National comparison test in Klasse 3 in German and Math, built on the Bildungsstandards.
One of five Math content areas in the Bildungsstandards (Zahlen und Operationen, Raum und Form, and so on).
Number wall: a pyramid of bricks where each brick is the sum of the two below; a standard German primary pattern task.
